title: FSD S6 reads the ACE views directly, while Architecture v5 allows only rwb-source-data to read them and gives S6 no cell to P1
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S6 Debt sale v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6); Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 13, 37 and 45; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1; Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1 DP-05
section: A1.1 constraints; A2.1, A2.2, A2.3, A2.6, A2.7, A2.12, A2.15, A2.16 integration points and validation rules
description: Sixteen features carry 'Data product stale after a late or failed ACE batch for its source (v_ace_batch_status)' as their first validation rule, A2.2 and A2.1 name the COLLINS lot economics read from v_ace_score and ACE (COLLINS scores ingested by ACE), A2.3 names 'ACE database, PII service', and A2.12 names 'ALS and GL' as a direct target. Architecture v5 slide 37 changes '30 views read by any module' to 'views read only by rwb-source-data', slide 45 answers 'who reads ACE data' with rwb-source-data alone, and the slide 13 connection matrix gives the S6 row no cell to P1 at all: its cells are Temporal to P7, P5, P8 and P2, events to and from P8, and events from P3. The account balance at cut-off, the COLLINS economics and the freshness therefore have no confirmed read path in any source.
evidence: FSD S6 A2.1 to A2.16 VR-S6-001-1 to VR-S6-016-1 (v_ace_batch_status); A2.1.2 and A2.2.2 integration points (ACE, COLLINS, v_ace_score); A2.3.2 integration point (ACE database, PII service). Arch v5 slide 13 (S6 row: T to P7, T to P5, T E to P8, T to P2, E from P3, no cell to P1); slide 37 (views read only by rwb-source-data); slide 45 (only rwb-source-data reads the 30 views; everyone else asks it through REST or a Temporal activity). Ownership Map: no view and no S6 row against rwb-source-data.
proposed: Carry the FSD field names (v_ace_score.*, v_ace_account.*, v_ace_batch_status.*) as the source field names the rwb-source-data contract returns, and build every read on that contract; no view and no ACE table is read here. Confirm the path with P1 (REST for the screen, activity inside the workflow) before the wave 3 system test.

title: The Ownership Map and the physical schema give this service two tables, while Architecture v5 gives it six things to hold
source: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 19 and 41; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 tables; Recovery Workbench Physical Schema v6; Recovery Workbench Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8
section: Slide 41 service catalogue; slide 19 S6 OUT line; A2.5, A2.8, A2.9, A2.13 field catalog
description: Architecture v5 slide 41 and slide 19 state that rwb-debtsale owns and writes 'lots, data room, buyer terms, bids, award, transfer'. The Ownership Map holds two S6 table rows only, debt_sale_lot and debt_sale_account, and the physical schema defines the same two; the data room state, the buyer terms, the bids, the award and the transfer have neither a table nor a field list. The FSD field catalog repeats the same eight debt_sale_lot fields in A2.5, A2.8, A2.9 and A2.13 and gives no field list for a bid, a term, an award or a transfer, so five of the six things the architecture gives this service cannot be built from the sources.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 41 (S6 rwb-debtsale: lots, data room, buyer terms, bids, award, transfer); slide 19 (DB writes schema rwb_debtsale: lots, data room, buyer terms, bids, award, transfer). Ownership Map Tables: debt_sale_lot, debt_sale_account (owner S6) and no other row. Physical Schema v6: CREATE TABLE debt_sale_lot, debt_sale_account only. FSD S6 A2.5.3.2, A2.8.3.2, A2.9.3.2, A2.13.3.2 (the same eight lot fields).
proposed: Hold the two named tables as physical tables and the other five as entity groups with the key fields this PRD states; fix the physical names with the S6 DB story and add the missing rows to the Ownership Map in the same change.

title: The physical schema keeps a foreign key from debt_sale_lot to partner, which sits in another service's schema
source: Recovery Workbench Physical Schema v6; Recovery Workbench Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 30 and 41; Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1 DP-01; Recovery Workbench Architecture Decision Records v3 ADR-014
section: A2.5.3.2 field catalog (debt_sale_lot.buyer_partner_id)
description: Physical Schema v6 writes ALTER TABLE debt_sale_lot ADD CONSTRAINT fk_debt_sale_lot_buyer_partner_id FOREIGN KEY (buyer_partner_id) REFERENCES partner (id), and creates ix_debt_sale_lot_buyer_partner_id. Under v5 the buyer panel is S9 rwb-partner's record in schema rwb_partner, and ADR-014 with DP-01 allow no cross-schema join and no foreign key out of the owner's schema; a link to another service's record is a business-key column with no foreign key. The same schema also carries debt_sale_account.account_key, which the Logical Data Model already flags as a business key against v_ace_account with no foreign key.
evidence: Physical Schema v6 line 2207 (FK debt_sale_lot.buyer_partner_id to partner), line 2307 (index on the same column), line 2208 (FK debt_sale_account.lot_id to debt_sale_lot, in-schema and allowed). LDM v8 DF-SAL-025 (buyer_partner_id, CROSS_REF, references partner) and DF-SAL-033 (account_key, business key against v_ace_account, no foreign key). Arch v5 slide 30 (19 schemas, one login each); ADR-014; Template and Rules DP-01.
proposed: Keep buyer_partner_id as a uuid business key with no foreign key and resolve the buyer through the S9 contract; the S6 migration creates no constraint that names a table outside rwb_debtsale.

title: The lot API is named /lots on slide 19 and /debt-sale-lots in the API specification, and no staff read of the bids exists
source: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 19; Recovery Workbench API Specification v4; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 API sheet; Recovery Workbench FSD S6 Debt sale v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) A2.8, A2.9
section: Slide 19 IN line; API Specification v4 /debt-sale-lots; A2.8 take buyer bids; A2.9 award
description: Architecture v5 slide 19 gives rwb-debtsale 'REST GET/POST /lots; POST /lots/{id}/bids to /award'. The API specification publishes five operations: POST /debt-sale-lots, GET /debt-sale-lots/{lotId}, POST /debt-sale-lots/{lotId}/award, GET /partner/data-room/{lotId} and POST /partner/data-room/{lotId}/bids. The Ownership Map records the API specification path for every row and cites slide 19 as the naming basis, so the two sources are recorded as agreeing on a path they name differently. No operation reads the bids of a lot for the staff screen, although A2.9 tests the best bid and SCR-26 shows bids against the reserve.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 19 (S6 IN: REST GET/POST /lots; POST /lots/{id}/bids /award). API Specification v4 lines 1786 to 1895 and 2739 to 2795 (five operations, x-module S6). Ownership Map API sheet rows citing 'slide 19 (rwb-debtsale IN: GET/POST /lots) names the path'. FSD S6 A2.8.2 (partner portal) and A2.9.2 (Workbench, partner portal).
proposed: Publish the API Specification v4 paths under /api/recovery/debtsale/v1 as the contract, carry the slide 19 /lots naming as the shorthand it is, and add the staff bid read to the contract when the S6 contract story closes.

title: The buyer data room is published under /partner, while the architecture admits buyers only through the partner gateway and S6 has no cell to S9
source: Recovery Workbench API Specification v4; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 13, 41 and 45 (ADR-019); Recovery Workbench FSD S6 Debt sale v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) Screens (PRT-05)
section: API Specification v4 /partner/data-room; A2.4 open the buyer data room; A2.8 take buyer bids; Screens
description: The API specification publishes the buyer operations as GET /partner/data-room/{lotId} and POST /partner/data-room/{lotId}/bids with x-module S6, and the FSD names the buyer screen PRT-05 as a partner portal screen first needed in E5. Architecture v5 puts every partner user behind the partner gateway in the DMZ with multi-factor authentication scoped to the partner's own records (ADR-019), and the slide 13 matrix gives rwb-partner a REST cell to the outside world but gives S6 no cell to S9 and no cell to a partner gateway. Who terminates the buyer's session, and whether the buyer calls this service directly through the partner gateway or through S9, is not stated in any source read.
evidence: API Specification v4 /partner/data-room/{lotId} and /partner/data-room/{lotId}/bids (x-module S6). Arch v5 slide 13 (S9 row: R to gateway-bff column and R to Outside; S6 row has no S9 and no Outside cell); slide 41 and 45 (partner gateway in the DMZ, adr-019); FSD S6 Screens (PRT-05 Data room, first in E5).
proposed: Publish the buyer operations from this service and expose them only through the partner gateway, with the buyer identity and its lot scope asserted by the gateway; confirm with the edge owner and S9 who terminates the partner session.

title: The customer notices of a sale have three different homes in three sources
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S6 Debt sale v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) A2.10; Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-DS-23; Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 22; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 19, 26 and 32
section: A2.10 generate the sale agreement and the notices; slide 22 step 7; slide 26 saga step 7
description: A2.10 gives its integration points as 'Workbench, WIN' and R-DS-23 says the award generates 'the sale agreement and the customer notices', but names no delivery path. The design's slide 22 lists 'Sold: close the case' as step 7 and its notes put 'tell customers (rwb-comms) after the pivot' in the saga, and architecture slide 26 gives step 7 as 'Tell customers  rwb-comms'. The slide 13 matrix gives the S6 row no cell to P6, and the only file path that exists is the WIN registered mail file INT-14 through rwb-integration. Three homes, one requirement.
evidence: FSD S6 A2.10.2 (integration points: Workbench, WIN); Business Rules v4 R-DS-23 (generate the sale agreement and the customer notices). Temporal and Drools Design slide 22 and its notes (the seven steps; tell customers rwb-comms); Arch v5 slide 26 (step 7 Tell customers rwb-comms); slide 13 (S6 row: no P6 cell); slide 32 (WIN letters 16:00, INT-14, through rwb-integration).
proposed: Send the customer notice through P6 rwb-comms via the workflow kit's Notify child and record the proof of delivery; keep the registered-mail file on P2 (INT-14). No direct WIN interface is opened by this service.

title: The buyer's KYC result, licence expiry and panel status have no owner and no source system
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S6 Debt sale v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) A2.6, A2.7; Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-DS-14, R-DS-15, R-DS-16, R-DS-40, R-DS-41; Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Epics 3 to 8 v1 Q-011, ASM-018; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1
section: A2.6 qualify a buyer against KYC and licensing; A2.7 bar a buyer; BRD Q-011
description: A2.6 and A2.7 require the KYC status, the licence expiry and the panel status of a bidder, and R-DS-15 reads kyc_status = passed, licence_expiry after today and panel_status = active. The FSD gives the integration points as 'Partner portal, Workbench' and names no system of record for any of the three facts. The BRD carries Q-011 open and assumes (ASM-018) that the bank's existing KYC and licensing checks apply, held as data. The Ownership Map gives the panel to S9 rwb-partner but has no row for a KYC result or a licence.
evidence: FSD S6 A2.6.2 and A2.7.2 integration points (Partner portal, Workbench); A2.6.3.1 and A2.7.3.1 rule rows. Business Rules v4 R-DS-14 to R-DS-16, R-DS-40, R-DS-41 (kyc_status, licence_expiry, panel_status). BRD Epics 3 to 8 v1 Q-011 and ASM-018; Program BRD v5 REQ-S6-004 and REQ-S6-005. Ownership Map: no KYC or licence row; S9 owns the panel.
proposed: Hold the KYC result, the licence expiry and the panel status as data on the buyer record, read the panel through the S9 contract, and record the evidence the officer accepted; confirm the source of the KYC and licence facts with Compliance before wave 4.

title: The debt sale cap has no basis and no period, only a figure
source: Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Epics 3 to 8 v1 Q-010, ASM-017, RULE-015; Recovery Workbench FSD S6 Debt sale v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) A2.1, A2.9, A2.16; Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 22
section: A2.1 select eligible accounts; A2.9 award and test the price; A2.16 apply the debt sale cap; BRD Q-010
description: Three features apply 'the 54 percent cap': A2.1 at selection, A2.9 in the price test, A2.16 in the cap position. None of them states what the 54 percent is a percentage of, over what period, or which role sets it; the BRD carries the question open (Q-010) and assumes (ASM-017) that the 54 percent applies to the eligible population of the period the policy names. The design's slide 22 repeats the figure without a basis. A cap applied to a different denominator is a different cap, and the headroom A2.16 reports is meaningless without one.
evidence: FSD S6 A2.1.3.1 (R-DS-01), A2.9.3.1 (R-DS-19), A2.16.1 (holds the population inside the policy cap and reports the headroom). BRD Epics 3 to 8 v1 Q-010, ASM-017, RULE-015, BR-050; Business Rules v4 R-DS-19 (54 percent cap). Temporal and Drools Design slide 22 ('inside the 54% cap').
proposed: Hold the cap, its denominator and its period as one versioned reference-data row with the role that owns it, and record the version applied at the selection, the award and the headroom report.

title: The approval bands in the design and the delegation in the FSD are two different statements of who approves an award
source: Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 22; Recovery Workbench FSD S6 Debt sale v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) A2.5, A2.9; Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-DS-06, R-DS-19; Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Epics 3 to 8 v1 Q-001; Decision Log v10 DL18
section: A2.5 approve lots, reserve and tiered terms; A2.9 award the lot; slide 22 'Who approves'
description: The FSD asks for approval 'inside the delegation' (R-DS-06) and 'with the approval the limit requires' (A2.9), and the design's slide 22 states the bands: secured, PARC if at or above 40 percent of FMV, else ExCo; unsecured, PARC if at or above 10 percent of principal, else ExCo. The delegation of authority matrix is open (DL18, BRD Q-001), so the bands exist in a design slide and nowhere in a versioned table, and the lot record's approval_authority is a free varchar(60).
evidence: FSD S6 A2.5.3.1 (R-DS-06, R-DS-07), A2.9.3.1 (R-DS-19), A2.5.3.2 (debt_sale_lot.approval_authority varchar(60)). Temporal and Drools Design slide 22 ('Who approves: Secured: PARC if at or above 40% FMV, else ExCo; Unsecured: PARC if at or above 10% principal, else ExCo'). Decision Log v10 DL18; BRD Epics 3 to 8 v1 Q-001.
proposed: Route the lot approval and the award through the P7 approval child on the delegation table of P4, hold the bands as versioned reference data with their valid-from date, and record the level applied and the approving role on the award; the free-text authority column then holds the level name, not a person.

title: Derecognition and the general ledger posting have no interface and no clear owner
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S6 Debt sale v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) A2.12, A2.14; Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-DS-30, R-DS-31, R-DS-32, R-DS-33; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 19, 26 and 41; Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v5 REQ-S6-008
section: A2.12 derecognize and post to the general ledger; A2.15 confirm buyer remittance
description: R-DS-30 'derecognise the balance on the account' and R-DS-31 'post to the general ledger and send the provision input to Finance' are written as Workbench actions with 'ALS core and GL' as their systems; A2.12 gives its integration points as 'ALS and GL'. Architecture v5 gives this service no cell to ALS, to the general ledger or to any outside system: its posting path is the activity payment.postProceeds on rwb-payment, and slide 26 puts 'Post proceeds rwb-payment' in the saga. Who actually derecognises, and where the posting file is built, is not stated.
evidence: FSD S6 A2.12.2 (integration points: ALS and GL); A2.12.3.1 (R-DS-30, R-DS-31, R-DS-33). Business Rules v4 R-DS-30 to R-DS-33. Arch v5 slide 19 (S6 OUT: TMP Payment: postProceeds); slide 26 (step 5 post proceeds, rwb-payment); slide 13 (S6 row: T E to P8 and no ALS or Outside cell). Program BRD v5 REQ-S6-008 (data transfer, derecognition and posting follow the award without re-keying).
proposed: Record the derecognition as this service's decision, have P8 build and send the posting and the provision input, and read the posted position back through the data path; no direct ALS or general ledger interface is opened here.

title: DebtSaleWorkflow is a saga per lot across five services, while the v5 case model is one child workflow per case per stage
source: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 25, 26 and 19; Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slides 13 and 22; Recovery Workbench FSD S6 Debt sale v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) A1.2, A2.1 to A2.16
section: Architecture slide 25 (a child per stage), slide 26 (the seven-step debt sale saga); FSD A2 step tables
description: Architecture v5 slide 25 makes CaseWorkflow the parent with one child per stage on the owner's queue, and slide 26 draws the debt sale as seven steps across five services with the transfer as the pivot, orchestrated by DebtSaleWorkflow in rwb-debtsale. The design's slide 22 note adds that 'S6 spans many cases at once; one sale event closes every case in the lot through a universal rule'. The FSD, however, writes each of its sixteen features as a step triggered per case ('Receives its trigger: a completed ACE batch, an event or a timer') and never states that a lot workflow spans cases. The parent and the orchestration are therefore described for two different units of work.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 25 (CaseWorkflow with a child per stage on the owner's queue; parent close policy ABANDON); slide 26 (the debt sale saga, pivot at transfer); slide 19 (S6 IN: DebtSaleWorkflow, saga, pivot = transfer). Temporal and Drools Design slide 13 (the four steps of every stage workflow) and slide 22 notes (S6 spans many cases at once). FSD S6 A2.1.2 to A2.16.2 step tables.
proposed: Run DebtSaleWorkflow as the stage workflow of the case that carries the eligibility and the case-side steps, and as the saga of the lot for the sale steps, with the lot identified by lot number; the case side is moved by rwb-case on LotAwarded and AccountsTransferred, never by a write into the case schema.

title: The monthly sale cycle has no schedule and no job row
source: Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 22; Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-DS-01; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 31 and 44; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 jobs
section: Slide 22 'Starts when the monthly sale cycle opens'; A2.1 step 1; A2.16
description: The design says the debt sale 'starts when the monthly sale cycle opens', R-DS-01 fires on DEBT_SALE_CYCLE_OPENED per monthly cycle, and the FSD's system features are triggered by 'a completed ACE batch, an event or a timer'. Architecture v5 replaces the shared scheduler with Temporal Schedules, and slide 31 lists them: rule promotion, measures, hash-chain check, smoke workflow, rebalancing and WIN letters. No schedule opens the sale cycle, and the Ownership Map jobs sheet holds 22 rows with no S6 row, so the trigger that starts the whole module has no owner and no name.
evidence: Temporal and Drools Design slide 22 ('Starts when the monthly sale cycle opens'); Business Rules v4 R-DS-01 (per monthly cycle, DEBT_SALE_CYCLE_OPENED). Arch v5 slide 31 (the Temporal Schedule list) and slide 44 (job map); slide 32 (the bank scheduler owns only the edges); Ownership Map Jobs sheet: no S6 row.
proposed: Open the cycle from a Temporal Schedule or an event-started workflow on rwb-debtsale through the workflow kit, name it in the job map with its owner and its run book, and record the cycle date it ran for.

title: AccountsTransferred has no event number and neither debt sale event has a published schema
source: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 42 and 43; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 events; Recovery Workbench FSD S6 Debt sale v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) A2.11, A2.14; Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v5 section 10.4
section: A2.11 transfer the data to the buyer; A2.14 close a case awarded in a sold lot
description: The event catalogue gives EV-23 LotAwarded a row with producer rwb-debtsale and consumers rwb-case and rwb-payment, and lists AccountsTransferred under the unnumbered 'plus' rows with rwb-case and rwb-reporting as consumers. EV-25 ProceedsMatched is the only event this service consumes. No AsyncAPI document, no CloudEvents schema and no payload field list exists for either debt sale event in the sources read, although the FSD requires the case steps to follow the award and the transfer.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 43 (row 23 LotAwarded; row 25 ProceedsMatched; '+' row AccountsTransferred with consumers rwb-case and rwb-reporting); Ownership Map Events: EV-23 only. Program BRD v5 section 10.4 (events are CloudEvents on rwb.<short>.events.v1 with an outbox and an inbox).
proposed: Publish both events as CloudEvents 1.0 on rwb.debtsale.events.v1 keyed by caseId, with BACKWARD-compatible schemas in the registry and no personal data in either; give AccountsTransferred its catalogue number under the same convention.

title: The PII service the tape depends on is not one of the 19 services and has no owner
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S6 Debt sale v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) A2.3; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 41 and 45; Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v5 NFR-041; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1
section: A2.3 prepare the masked data tape; Existing capability check
description: A2.3 gives 'ACE database, PII service' as its integration points and its masking rules are R-DS-10 (build the tape under the PII masking rules), R-DS-11 (reject the tape when an unmasked identifier is found) and R-DS-12 (rebuild). NFR-041 makes the masked tape a non-functional requirement. The 19 services contain no masking service: the masking policy is P4 rwb-access's (permission, scope, masking policy), the PII logging path is ACE common's, and the tape as a document is P5's. Nothing states who performs the masking.
evidence: FSD S6 A2.3.2 integration points (ACE database, PII service); A2.3.3.1 (R-DS-10, R-DS-11, R-DS-12). Arch v5 slide 41 (the 19 services; P4 owns the masking policy; P5 owns documents); slide 45; Program BRD v5 NFR-041; Ownership Map: no masking row.
proposed: Read the masking rules from P4 as versioned policy data, mask inside this service before the tape becomes a P5 document, and make the masking check a release gate with its result recorded on the tape record.

title: The model gateway and the lot agent estimate have no owner among the 19 services
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S6 Debt sale v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) A2.2; Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-DS-04; Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 12 (the analyst's kit) and slide 22; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1
section: A2.2 build the lots and estimate the price; slide 12 'Agent run with rule fallback'; slide 22 'R-DS-04 COLLINS'
description: A2.2 names 'Model gateway' as an integration point, and R-DS-04 fires on 'lot agent estimate returned with COLLINS' and hands the proposal to the committee. The design's slide 12 lists the kit's 'Agent run with rule fallback' and its notes apply it to 'the route agent and pricing agent (R-UNI-32)'. No feature of this FSD is an agent capability, no requirement of REQ-S6-001 to REQ-S6-009 mentions an agent, the Ownership Map has no agent row for S6, and there is no service called model gateway: the agent runtime is P10 rwb-agent and the model endpoint is outside the bank.
evidence: FSD S6 A2.2.2 integration points (ACE, Model gateway); Business Rules v4 R-DS-04 (lot agent estimate returned with COLLINS). Temporal and Drools Design slide 12 (Agent run with rule fallback) and its notes (route agent and pricing agent); slide 22. Arch v5 slide 41 (P10 rwb-agent holds agent policies, prompts, runs and guardrails); no model gateway row in the Ownership Map.
proposed: Where an agent contributes to the lot estimate, run it through the P10 contract with the kit's agent run, a 60 s limit and the rule result as the fallback, and record the agent, model and prompt versions with the estimate; otherwise compute the estimate from the COLLINS economics by rule.

title: Two state vocabularies describe the same lot: the routing ladder and the status list
source: Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-DS-01 to R-DS-41; Recovery Workbench Physical Schema v6; Recovery Workbench Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8 debt_sale_lot.status and LOV-LOT-STATUS
section: A2.1 to A2.16 rule rows (LOT_BUILT, TAPE_PREPARED, BIDS_RECEIVED, LOT_AWARDED, LOT_CLOSED); field catalog status
description: The routing rules move a lot through a ladder of about twenty states (LOT_CANDIDATE_SELECTED, LOT_BUILT, LOT_PRICED, LOT_WITH_COMMITTEE, LOT_APPROVED, TAPE_PREPARED, DATA_ROOM_OPEN, BIDDING_OPEN, BIDS_RECEIVED, AWARD_PENDING, LOT_AWARDED, SETTLEMENT_PENDING, SETTLED, DATA_TRANSFERRED, DERECOGNISED, GL_POSTED, PUTBACK_RAISED, LOT_CLOSED and the exception states). The physical schema holds a status varchar(12) with LOV-LOT-STATUS 'Building, offered, awarded, transferred, closed' and a separate state varchar(40). Nothing states which of the two the workflow state machine writes, or which one the screen shows.
evidence: Business Rules v4 R-DS-01 to R-DS-41 (the state ladder). Physical Schema v6 lines 422 to 424 (status varchar(12) default BUILDING, state varchar(40)) and LDM v8 DF-SAL-030 (LOV-LOT-STATUS: Building, offered, awarded, transferred, closed). FSD S6 A2.1.3.1 and A2.10.3.1 rule rows naming moves such as 'Moves to LOT_BUILT'.
proposed: Use the routing ladder as the workflow state written to state, and the five-value LOV as the business status the screen shows; record both on the lot and never infer one from the other.

title: borrower_code and account_key are flagged not personal in the data model, yet they identify a customer on the tape
source: Recovery Workbench Physical Schema v6; Recovery Workbench Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8 DF-SAL-033 and DF-SAL-034; Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v5 NFR-039 and NFR-041; Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Epics 3 to 8 v1 RISK-005
section: A2.3 prepare the masked data tape; field catalog debt_sale_account
description: The Logical Data Model records DF-SAL-033 account_key and DF-SAL-034 borrower_code with is_personal = false, and the physical schema's sys_fields rows agree. Both fields identify the customer whose debt is being sold, and the tape and the transfer file are the two artefacts this module sends outside the bank. NFR-041 requires the tape to be masked before it reaches the data room, NFR-039 requires party identifiers to be masked by role, and RISK-005 is 'debt sale personal data leaves the bank unmasked'. A mask list that reads the personal flag would leave both fields in clear.
evidence: Physical Schema v6 lines 3855 to 3863 (sys_fields rows for DF-SAL-021 to DF-SAL-029 with is_personal false) and LDM v8 rows DF-SAL-033 and DF-SAL-034 (both is_personal No). Program BRD v5 NFR-039, NFR-040, NFR-041. BRD Epics 3 to 8 v1 RISK-005 and section 6 row 6.
proposed: Treat borrower_code and account_key as personal data in use, mask both on every screen and on the tape and the transfer file by role, and correct the is_personal flag in the next version of the Logical Data Model and the physical schema.

title: The three screens have no owner in the sources read
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S6 Debt sale v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) Screens; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 41 and 45 and the gateway notes; Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1 DP-19
section: Screens (SCR-25 Lot builder, SCR-26 Award, PRT-05 Data room); Architecture edge and gateway
description: The FSD names three screens and their first release, and no source read states which application serves them or which service holds the screen definition. Architecture v5 puts staff screens behind gateway-bff composite routes (one hop, calls in parallel, screens never chain calls) and partner screens behind the partner gateway, and DP-19 gives the composite route to the platform edge; there is no screen-ownership matrix in the extract for these three screens, so who builds SCR-25 and SCR-26 is an open item.
evidence: FSD S6 Screens table (SCR-25 Lot builder, SCR-26 Award, PRT-05 Data room, first in E5 and E6). Arch v5 slide 41 (services and the edge); the gateway notes on composite routes and 'screens never chain calls'; Template and Rules DP-19 (gateway-bff composite route). No screen matrix row for SCR-25, SCR-26 or PRT-05 in the Architecture v5 extract.
proposed: Serve SCR-25 and SCR-26 through gateway-bff composite routes and PRT-05 through the partner gateway, with this service publishing only data and commands; name the screen owner in the edge story.

title: No source states who owns the wording of the debt sale messages and their Thai and English versions
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S6 Debt sale v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) A2.1 to A2.16; Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1 R8.5; Recovery Workbench Error and Message Standard (referenced by FSD Appendix B); Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v5 NFR-059
section: A2.1.3.1 to A2.16.3.1 message column; Appendix B
description: The FSD uses MSG-S6-001 (an account with an open deviation cannot be sold) and the shared MSG-P1-001, MSG-P4-002, MSG-P7-003 and MSG-GEN-001, and its Appendix B says message wording follows the Error and Message Standard. No source read names the owner of the wording, the approval path for a new message, or who confirms the Thai and English versions that NFR-059 requires.
evidence: FSD S6 A2.11.3.1, A2.13.3.1 and A2.14.3.1 (MSG-S6-001, MSG-P4-002), A2.1.3.1 to A2.16.3.1 (MSG-P1-001, MSG-GEN-001, MSG-P7-003), Appendix B (message wording follows the Error and Message Standard). Program BRD v5 NFR-059.
proposed: Carry MSG-S6-001 and the four shared messages in the message catalogue with a named owner and a Thai and English version, and confirm the wording before wave 4.

title: The FSD's prerequisite feature codes belong to four other modules and two of its own features are missing from its dependency list
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S6 Debt sale v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) A1.1 dependencies and the Prerequisites line of A2.1, A2.3, A2.5 and A2.10; FSD P1, P6 and P7 v3/v4
section: A1.1 dependencies; Prerequisites of A2.1 (FEAT-DRI-07), A2.3 (FEAT-RDF-15), A2.5 (FEAT-APD-01), A2.10 (FEAT-OCC-07)
description: A1.1 lists FEAT-APD-01 and seven of this module's own features as dependencies, and the Prerequisites line of four features names FEAT-DRI-07 (P7 rwb-decision: run the rules component on versioned rule tables), FEAT-RDF-15 (P1 rwb-source-data: access control per data product for PDPA), FEAT-APD-01 (P7: route a recommendation to the approver by limit) and FEAT-OCC-07 (P6 rwb-comms: generate contract, credit approval and mortgage documents). None of the four is defined in this FSD, and under v5 each is another service's capability reached through its contract. A2.5 and A2.16, which the FSD also depends on, are absent from the A1.1 list.
evidence: FSD S6 A1.1 dependencies (FEAT-APD-01; FEAT-DBS-01; FEAT-DBS-03; FEAT-DBS-04; FEAT-DBS-06; FEAT-DBS-08; FEAT-DBS-09; FEAT-DBS-11); A2.1.2, A2.3.2, A2.5.2 and A2.10.2 prerequisites. FSD P7 Decision center and log v3 (FEAT-DRI-07, FEAT-APD-01), FSD P1 Recovery data engine v3 (FEAT-RDF-15), FSD P6 Communications v3 (FEAT-OCC-07).
proposed: Map each prerequisite to the owning service's contract as a contract dependency (P7 for the rules component and the approval routing, P1 for access control per data product, P6 for the template set), and add FEAT-DBS-05 and FEAT-DBS-16 to the dependency list when the stories are written.

title: Retention, classification and the masking rules a record is held under are open
source: Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v5 NFR-028, NFR-031, NFR-047, DL26; Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Epics 3 to 8 v1 Q-012; Recovery Workbench Physical Schema v6 (no retention class)
section: Section 8 data requirements; A2.3 masked tape
description: DL26 is open and Q-012 asks what the retention periods and masking rules are by record class and by role. NFR-047 requires a classification on every data product and document type but records it as open, NFR-028 and NFR-031 leave the periods unset, and the physical schema carries no retention class column. This module holds the sale population, the bids and the tape, which are the records a retention rule and a data subject request will be tested against.
evidence: Program BRD v5 NFR-028, NFR-031, NFR-047 and DL26; BRD Epics 3 to 8 v1 Q-012; Physical Schema v6 debt_sale_lot and debt_sale_account (no retention class column); LDM v8 DP09 data product row with no retention period.
proposed: Give every record a data classification and a retention class and hold the periods as reference data from DL26; apply the class to the tape and to the transfer file through P5 and P2, which own the document and the file.

title: The put-back window, the remediation window and the settlement term are not stated and are business values
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S6 Debt sale v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) A2.7, A2.11, A2.13, A2.15; Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-DS-24, R-DS-27, R-DS-34, R-DS-35, R-DS-40; Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 22 clocks; Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v5 DL22
section: A2.7 bar a buyer; A2.11 transfer; A2.13 put-back; A2.15 remittance
description: R-DS-35 opens a ten working day window for a put-back review, R-DS-40 gives the buyer ten working days to supply evidence, R-DS-24 starts a settlement term 'per agreed settlement period' and R-DS-34 closes the lot 'per claim window'. The FSD itself says only 'inside the window', 'inside the claim window' and 'inside the settlement period'. The design's slide 22 puts 'put-back review and remediation 10 wd' in its clocks and DL22 makes every state service level a parameter. A window with no value is a rule that cannot be tested.
evidence: Business Rules v4 R-DS-24, R-DS-27, R-DS-34, R-DS-35, R-DS-40. FSD S6 A2.7.3.1 (R-DS-40), A2.11.3.1 (R-DS-25), A2.13.3.1 (R-DS-34), A2.15.3.1 (R-DS-25, R-DS-26). Temporal and Drools Design slide 22 ('Clocks: monthly cycle; put-back review and remediation 10 wd'). Program BRD v5 DL22.
proposed: Hold the three windows as versioned reference-data rows with their valid-from dates, apply the value in force at the business date of the lot, and record the version applied on the claim and the settlement.
